text:
julia: Heads-up — I'd like to propose a 'tombstone' flow in the console/editor so deleting config keys isn't destructive. Idea: soft-delete (tombstone) + audit entry + scheduled sweep job. Thoughts?
sam: big +1. accidental deletes have bitten us in staging.
maria: can we tie tombstone -> automatic rollback window? keep config around for X days and provide 'undelete' button.
david: ops concern: sweep must be gated. For keys referenced by routing/quotas we can't auto-sweep. Need dependency check.
julia: agree. propose states: active -> tombstoned (soft-delete, hidden by default) -> eligible-for-sweep -> swept (hard delete). show in UI with orange badge.
nate: what about retention default? 30 days feels short. I'd vote 90 days for enterprise.
maria: 90 for enterprise, 30 for normal — add override via policy.
ops-bot: deploy-job:created sweep-run dryrun=true --filter tombstone=true
sam: also need audit events and reversible mutation id. Add tombstone_id uuid so rollback-api can reinstate.
david: dependency check is tricky: run static analysis + runtime lookups. We should at least block sweep if referenced by any active route or quota.
julia: UX: show "blocked-by" list in editor and let owner request exception. Also a "request-sweep" flow for SRE.
maria: logs — push to kafka topic config.tombstone.events with {id, user, ts, refs}. retention 365d.
nate: add a dry-run CLI: rctl config sweep --dry-run --since 2026-01-01
sam: tests: create e2e fixture where tombstone->undelete->sweep triggers error and ensure alerting.
david: policy: if sweep deletes >100 keys at once require 2nd approver.
julia: sounds good. I'll draft RFC and a console mock. Anyone want to pair on the mock tomorrow?
maria: I can.
sam: me too. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: scheduled: config-tombstone-rfc-draft created by julia at 5901234567
julia: thanks all — will ping the product PM for policy signoff. :eyes:
